articles.title: The rise of hairy young women: ‘I know people who dye their armpit hair, so it stands out more’
articles.summary: When Phoebe Bridgers appeared at Venice international film festival with unshaven legs this weekend, it shouldn’t have made headlines – but did. What do young women make of the current expectations around depilation? In 2026, female body hair feels as if it should be the least of anyone’s concerns.
body: Even so, her au naturel look may signal that attitudes are changing – particularly among younger generations. Vogue decreed that “rather than undermining the femininity of the look, unapologetic hair sharpened it”, and pictures of the 32-year-old’s hair-covered calves were generally praised by fans. But what do other gen Z and millennial women make of the decision to ditch the razor?

“Hell yeah!” is 27-year-old PhD student Anna Busuttil’s response. “I think it’s awesome; cool and rebellious,” she says – a view that chimes with that of most of the women I speak to outside University College London’s Bloomsbury campus. Busuttil says she sees a lot more women nowadays choosing not to remove their body hair. “I know people who dye their armpit hair a certain colour as well, so it stands out even more. I feel like leg hair is more taboo for women; it feels like such a ‘masculine’ thing, and legs are supposed to be a really sexy part of a woman.”
points: What do young women make of the current expectations around depilation?
In 2026, female body hair feels as if it should be the least of anyone’s concerns.

articles.title: Jibby Beane obituary
articles.summary: My glamorous friend Jibby Beane, who has died aged 84, was known in London’s fashion and art worlds as an energetic and unique figure. Blessed with fabulous blond good looks, during the 1990s she appeared on the catwalk for Vivienne Westwood, was featured in countless style magazines and ran an art…
body: Wherever Jibby arrived, laced into a Westwood corset and tottering on platform shoes, everyone knew who she was. She had started modelling in the 60s and appeared in the first Andrex television commercial to feature a labrador retriever puppy in 1972. She had also worked for the couturier Victor Stiebel. In 1963 she married Kenneth Beane, whom she had known since childhood.

Talented at decorating houses, and selling them, she studied interior design and got a diploma from Richmond Adult College in the late 80s. She went on to establish her own company, Dream Designs, and worked occasionally at the Design and Decoration Building in Chelsea, where she was a greeter; there she met Westwood in the ladies’ loos. She had also met a young art student, Jonathan Goslan, in 1991, which led to her separation from Ken.

By 1992, Jibby was the face of Westwood’s Mayfair stores, holding court every Saturday as she slipped into one outfit after another. “She seemed to have multiple sides – from diva to comedian,” said Mark Garcia, a colleague. “But my favourite was the one she called ‘Mother Beane’. If you needed advice, or comfort, or reassurance, she would give it all. She was incredibly kind.”
points: My glamorous friend Jibby Beane, who has died aged 84, was known in London’s fashion and art worlds as an energetic and unique figure.

articles.title: Alice Zaslavsky’s satay-butter charred cabbage wedges with fragrant chicken mince – recipe
articles.summary: The cookbook author has a shortcut method for blanching vegetables that saves on time, equipment and water. Check out more Alice Zaslavsky recipes. I love a burnt brassica, and there’s no better flavour than the big mama herself: the cabbage.
body: Vegetables in the cruciferous family, like brussels sprouts, broccoli and cauliflower, have naturally bitter compounds. However, with concentrated heat, this bitterness is transformed into sweetly caramelised corners and burnished bits.
It’s one way to make brassica boo-ers braver. But getting cooked-through cabbage with a softened heart and gnarly edges requires a delicate balance of time under heat.

Lucky for us, the sharp bitterness of cabbage has been bred out of more conventional styles on supermarket and greengrocer shelves. Modern varieties are much milder, sweeter and less fibrous, meaning they require far less cooking than the cabbages of old.
That’s why these days, I’m fond of a gentler method that softens their rawness without overcooking: the kettle-blanch.

I love a burnt brassica, and there’s no better flavour than the big mama herself: the cabbage.

Making cafe-caliber java at home is possible with these six coffee-making upgrades. Sign up for the Filter US newsletter, your weekly guide to buying fewer, better things.
body: Soft serve always feels like a special occasion. While I can open a pint of Ben & Jerry’s any old time, fresh soft serve conjures memories of childhood visits to TCBY and the McDonalds drive through. As an adult in New York, I now associate it with my daughter’s squeals of excitement when she hears the Mister Softee truck jingling down the block. And as more of my peers pull back from alcohol, meeting a friend for a froyo and stroll has become a satisfying stand-in for happy hour.

Naturally I’m thrilled to see soft serve has enjoyed a renaissance, especially in my city. Last year, cronut creator Dominique Ansel made waves with soft serve dipped in French butter. Soft serve margaritas took over TikTok this year. And if line culture is any indication of interest, soft serve spots like Culture and, in my neighborhood, Lisbonata, now draw round-the-block throngs of treat seekers.

articles.summary: Two months after their mega-wedding at Madison Square Garden, Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce stepped out for dinner in New York wearing coordinating shimmers.
body: The couple opted to dine at a Swiftian-favorite, the Ambassadors Clubhouse in NoMad, for their first NYC date night post-nuptials.
Her glam was signature; Swift sported her freshly cut lob and wore it curled with her bangs blown sleek and straight, with a trending aqua blue manicure, matte red lip, and flick of black eyeliner.

Kelce, meanwhile, kept to his usual silhouette: he wore a shiny silk, striped short-sleeved Amiri shirt with brown tailored pants and checkered Vans slip-ons (sans socks), adding aviator shades and a gold watch.
Swift’s most recent appearance was on a girls night out in London.

articles.title: The Bride Mirrored Her Mother’s Wedding Day Looks at Her Backyard Wedding in Santa Barbara
articles.summary: Sarah Hancock married Matthew Conaghan in a Danielle Frankel gown that she says “made me feel like Grace Kelly,” with a celebration at the bride’s family home that combined California nostalgia and coastal sophistication.
body: The bride had her mother, interior designer Emily Hancock, as a partner throughout the planning process as well. “I loved our dynamic because while we have the same taste, she appreciated where we differed and respected that rather than trying to overtake the process,” says Sarah. “She saw my vision and enhanced it.” The groom also got involved in the design process. “He completely owned the vision of the rehearsal dinner with his parents and did an incredible job,” she adds.

For the welcome party at the Valley Club of Montecito, Sarah wanted to wear a large bow similar to her mother’s wedding day accessory. “When a friend tipped me off about Kamperett, a San Francisco-based designer, I found both the bow and the slip dress to go with it,” she says. A month ahead of the wedding, she found a soft pink shrug from WoolHouse to top off the look along with blush Manolo Blahnik heels. “My jewelry was designed by Aaron Henry, a local jewelry designer based in downtown Los Angeles who also helped me design my engagement ring,” she shares.

articles.title: Just One Thing: Meet Cartier’s New Clash de Cartier Bag
articles.summary: Blurring the line between leather goods and jewelry, Cartier’s new Clash de Cartier bag turns one of the maison’s signature studs into its defining clasp.
body: Deciding between a new piece of jewelry or a new bag? Cartier would rather you didn’t have to choose. The maison’s newly launched Clash de Cartier bag is essentially both, borrowing its defining detail from the Clash de Cartier jewelry collection.

The debut tote, introduced globally on September 1, 2026 and available in three sizes, is defined by two jewelry clasps positioned on either side of its handle, each modeled after the signature stud of Clash de Cartier (the jewelry collection, introduced in 2019, is known for its geometric studs, beads, and clous carrés ). With a simple twist, the studs open and close the sides of the bag, allowing its envelope-inspired silhouette to shift along with them: left open, it’s softer and more relaxed; fastened, more tailored and structured.

articles.title: Fashion Forecast: A Psychic, Astrologer, and Tarot Reader Predict Fall Trends
articles.summary: We're gazing in our crystal ball to see what we'll be wearing in the months ahead.
body: While putting on a trench or light sweater is still mostly wishful thinking—the hot, humid temps of summer always stick around longer than they’re wanted—now’s the time to start talking about fall fashion. In these transitional months, everyone has their own premonitions about what trends will dominate the season ahead, but what will actually happen is pretty much anyone’s guess. So we tapped a few people, including some ast with closer connections to destiny to tell us what the future might hold for fashion.

David Scoroposki is an astrologer and former Vogue editor. While at Vogue, he edited an astrology column by the anonymous “Athena Starwoman,” he said, so, he’s particularly qualified to prognosticate in these pages.

When he looked to the stars, he found, “As Venus reigns supreme in her own sign of Libra, dressing now centers on harmonious beauty and unabashed finery,” said Scoroposki. “Venus is the ultimate astrological signifier for fashion, and in her home placement, the focus returns to flattering silhouettes, exquisite textiles, and romantic tailoring that draws subtle attention to the lower back and waistline, especially.”
points: We're gazing in our crystal ball to see what we'll be wearing in the months ahead.
